newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila wheat buyers scamper away on peso fall.
newsitem.headline: Manila wheat buyers scamper away on peso fall.

text.p: Philippine wheat importers, scared by the drop of the peso to a record low on Monday, are expected to stay away from the market despite softer U.S. wheat prices, Manila grains traders said.
"The peso fall will definitely temper our buying intentions," an executive in a Philippine flour mill told Reuters.
Philippine flour mills flocked to the U.S. wheat market last week after prices fell due to a report by the U.S. Department of Agriculture of higher production estimates for the year.
On Tuesday, the USDA raised its estimate of 1997/1998 U.S. wheat production to 68.87 million tonnes, up more than 2.50 million in 1996/1997.
U.S. wheat prices dropped following the announcement, prompting Philippine wheat buyers to buy up to 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat in three separate transctions last week, traders said.
On Friday, Philippine mills bought at auction 30,000 tonnes dark northern spring with 14 percent protein content and 5,000 tonnes western white wheat, traders said.
Two other groups bought a total 65,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat last Wednesday.

"I had expected more mills to book forward orders this week because of softer U.S. wheat prices. That prospect seemed to have dimmed because of the drop in the peso," a senior Manila grains trader said.
Philippine mills have stepped up wheat buying at the start of this month due to lower prices and the slight recovery of the peso, traders said.
Local buyers had so far bought a total 267,000 tonnes wheat, including 100,000 tonnes Canadian wheat, since the start of the month. This included last week's transactions, traders said.
Philippine wheat buyers were mostly sidelined last month after the peso plunged by more than 11 percent following its de facto devaluation on July 11.
The peso slumped to a record low 30.10 against the dollar in early trade on Monday from the previous close of 29.80.
